papers.title: Complex magnetism in a transition metal nitride
papers.authors: Dominik Werhahn, S. Steinberg, Clemens Ritter, Felix Drötboom, J. Paul Attfield, Simon D. Kloß
papers.abstract: Abstract High-symmetry lattices of transition metal ions such as the body-centred tetragonal (bct) arrangement are model systems for correlated electron physics and frustrated magnetism. Transition metal oxides or halides with the bct K 2 NiF 4 -type structure are extensively studied and have ground states dominated by strong interactions within the square layers, but materials exemplifying other bct ground states are much rarer. Here we show that Ca 2 CoN 2 , from the underexplored class of transition metal nitrides, has one of the complex magnetic ground states predicted for the bct lattice lying close to a spin-liquid instability. Ca 2 CoN 2 has been synthesised at high pressure in a large-volume press, and has a Na 2 HgO 2 -type structure where weakening of intralayer superexchange interactions leads to frustration. Our magnetisation and neutron diffraction experiments reveal an incommensurate spin order below 54 K, consistent with a double- k spin density wave with propagation vectors ( k 00) and (0 k 0) where k = 0.57. This phase lies close to the predicted crossover (at k = 0.64–0.69) to a modulated spin liquid, which could be explored through further chemical tuning. This work demonstrates the potential of transition metal nitrides as magnetic model systems, alongside the much-studied oxides and halides, for exploring complex spin orders and associated quantum phases.
papers.summary_en: This work identifies an incommensurate magnetic ground state in high-pressure-synthesized Ca₂CoN₂, a transition-metal nitride with a body-centred tetragonal lattice. The observed order lies near a theoretically predicted crossover toward a modulated spin liquid, motivating chemical tuning of the material.

papers.title: Spinless Charged Excitation at the Interface between a Conventional Topological Insulator and a Topological Mott Insulator
papers.authors: Cesar A. Gallegos, Andrew J. Millis, Steven R. White
papers.abstract: We investigate the interface separating two topologically distinct insulating phases of matter using extensive density-matrix renormalization group calculations to study the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model with a spatially varying interaction strength, chosen to realize both integer quantum Hall and chiral spin liquid states in different spatial regions. We find that the integer quantum Hall-chiral spin liquid interface hosts a spinless charged excitation that is bound to the interface. This mode at the interface is identified through charge and spin pumping, and by direct calculations of low-lying excited states. We also characterize bulk excitations in both phases, finding evidence for fractionalization in the chiral spin liquid and for spin-triplet exciton formation in the integer quantum Hall phase.

papers.title: Nonlinear Phononic Slidetronics
papers.authors: Pooja Rani, Dominik M. Juraschek
papers.abstract: Layered van der Waals ferroelectrics are conventionally switched by sliding the different layers between stacking orders with opposing electric polarizations. Ultrashort laser pulses have been proposed to launch shear modes and induce switching, with often unfeasible large pulse energies, however. Here, we demonstrate switching of ferroelectricity in bilayer hexagonal boron nitride through nonlinearly excited phonons. We show that the efficiencies of conventional coherent phonon excitation mechanisms, including infrared absorption and Raman scattering techniques, are too low to overcome the energy barrier separating the two ferroelectric states. We demonstrate instead that excitation of high-frequency intralayer modes leads to a tilting of the interlayer potential-energy landscape that enables changing the stacking order. Our results provide an avenue toward efficient phononic slidetronics, enabling ultrafast control of the stacking order in van der Waals materials.
papers.summary_en: This paper demonstrates a proposed route to switch ferroelectricity in bilayer hexagonal boron nitride by exciting phonons nonlinearly. It reports that high-frequency intralayer modes tilt the interlayer energy landscape and enable a stacking change, whereas conventional coherent-phonon excitation mechanisms are too inefficient to overcome the switching barrier.

papers.abstract: Optically driven chiral phonons can induce transient magnetism in non-magnetic crystals, yet the microscopic relationship between phonon angular momentum and the resulting magnetic response remains unresolved. Here we distinguish the roles of pseudo-angular momentum and mechanical angular momentum in tetragonal α-TeO2. Combining phase-resolved terahertz spectroscopy with magneto-optical Kerr measurements (MOKE), we reconstruct the motion of a doubly degenerate phonon and continuously control its angular momentum. The MOKE response follows the sign and magnitude of phonon angular momentum as well as its dynamics, whereas non-rotating phonons, including those with finite pseudo-angular momentum, produce no detectable magnetic signal. The MOKE rotation corresponds to an effective magnetic field of approximately 14 mT, nearly seven orders of magnitude above the estimate for spatially uniform ionic currents. Moreover, the Kerr response scales linearly with the emitted terahertz field, rather than quadratically as predicted by the uniform-current model. A localized Raman-excitation model involving Te lone-pair states accounts for this scaling and yields a comparable field magnitude with the MOKE data when electronic enhancement is included. These findings identify mechanical lattice rotation as the dominant dynamical variable for the observed magnetic response and suggest that localized Raman coupling contributes to its unexpectedly large magnitude.

papers.relevance_reason: The measurements and modeling establish a distinctive coupling between lattice angular momentum and transient magnetism in a crystal, a substantial condensed-matter result.

papers.abstract: Correlations and topology are central pillars in the study of emergent electronic phases. Topological flat bands near the Fermi level unite these concepts, providing a route towards correlated topological phenomena and unconventional magnetism. Despite theoretical predictions, momentum-resolved observation of a topological flat band at the Fermi level has remained elusive. Using angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we observe a flat band at the Fermi level within the topologically non-trivial electronic structure of the magnetic kagome Weyl semimetal Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$. We further uncover a strong temperature dependence in which the flat band shifts across the Fermi level, accompanied by a reconstruction of the Fermi surface. Strikingly, this evolution occurs on the same temperature scale as previously reported anomalies in the magnetic response. Together, these results provide evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$, establishing a microscopic setting in which topology, electronic correlations, and magnetism become intertwined.

papers.abstract: We performed Shubnikov--de Haas (SdH) oscillation measurements on the $\mathbf{Q}=0$ antiferromagnet NbMnP, which exhibits a large anomalous Hall effect. The SdH frequencies observed in the low-field region up to 17.5~T are well described by first-principles band-structure calculations based on the $B_{3g}+B_{2u}$ noncollinear magnetic structure determined by neutron diffraction. The effective masses are enhanced by approximately a factor of two relative to the calculated band masses. High-field measurements up to 41.5~T reveal a Lifshitz transition accompanied by a pronounced evolution of the SdH frequency spectrum. These results confirm that first-principles calculations provide a reliable tool for the development of functional antiferromagnetic materials, while also demonstrating that field-induced changes in the Fermi surface itself need to be taken into account in understanding their high-field magnetotransport properties.

papers.relevance_reason: Quantum-oscillation measurements reveal a field-induced Fermi-surface transition in a noncollinear antiferromagnet, providing a substantive result on magnetic electronic structure.

papers.abstract: Chiral magnetic materials can host skyrmions and hence are of interest for numerous spintronic applications including low-power storage. To reach this goal, room temperature operation and a thin film form are needed. We have studied the chiral magnetism in a $β$-Mn structured CoZn sputtered film, with a Curie temperature of $\approx 130$ °C, by means of polarized neutron reflectometry (PNR) in order to reveal its magnetic field-temperature phase diagram. papers.abstract: Topological orders in realistic systems are quite rare, raising one fundamental question of whether they might be harbored with hidden degrees of freedom rather than directly exposed in conventional spins or electrons. We here propose a set of hidden variables and their effective interactions in a bilayer kagomé antiferromagnet. By properly organizing four local states of the spin dimer into two pseudospin-$1/2$ variables ($\boldsymbolτ$ and $\boldsymbolμ$), we identify a regime where an effective Balents-Fisher-Girvin model emerges, realizing a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order in the hidden $\boldsymbolτ$ sector while the auxiliary $\boldsymbolμ$ sector remains a trivial paramagnet. This hidden nature drastically alters the experimental manifestations. Physical spins map to composite objects, typically convolving fractionalized anyon continua with non-topological magnon excitations. Nevertheless, specific symmetry-selected channels, such as the longitudinal intralayer response, exclusively reveal the bare two-vison continuum without collective-mode dressing. Our findings demonstrate that the topological order could be buried in certain hidden and emergent degrees of freedom, pointing to a promising pathway for seeking elusive topological states disguised within hidden internal degrees of freedom.

papers.abstract: The quantum Hall interferometer has been shown to be a powerful tool for probing both the nature of the chiral modes present at the edges of these systems and the interactions between them. Strong inter-edge mode interactions can lead the system into a regime where the period of the interferometer signal corresponds to an insertion of a half-quantum flux h/2e, rather than the standard flux quantum h/e. Using a highly tunable bilayer graphene device, we are able to measure the prevalence of both the h/e-period and the doubled-frequency regimes as a function of magnetic field, providing insight into the microscopic nature of the doubling mechanism. Furthermore, we are able to push our device to a regime where double-frequency oscillations coexist with a superimposed period-h/e pattern associated with the inner chiral modes farther from the edge. We argue that this regime has a natural interpretation in a picture of the frequency doubling being caused by strong capacitive couplings between the edge modes.

papers.abstract: Strain-tuned $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ thin films provide a model system for controlling coupled valence, spin-state, structural and metal-insulator transitions (VSSTs) in perovskite cobaltite materials. In compressively strained films on YAlO$_{3}$ (YAO) substrates, cooling through the transition produces Pr$^{4+}$-like spectral weight, suppresses Co$^{4+}$-like character, and favors predominantly low-spin Co$^{3+}$. The changes at the Pr and Co edges are quantitatively consistent with a reduction of approximately 0.15 holes per Co in the Co--O network. By contrast, tensile-strained thin films on La$_{0.18}$Sr$_{0.82}$Al$_{0.59}$Ta$_{0.41}$O$_{3}$ (LSAT) substrates have nearly temperature-independent spectra. Multiplet calculations reproduce the principal XAS lineshapes and local $dd$ excitations at high energy loss. Additionally, low-energy RIXS intensity recovered above the transition is consistent with a combination of Co$^{4+}$-like local excitations and a broader particle--hole continuum associated with the metallic phase. These results provide element-resolved evidence for charge compensation between the Pr and Co--O sublattices and support cooperative coupling among charge-transfer, spin-state, and lattice structure at the strain-controlled VSST.

papers.abstract: Altermagnets are a unique subset of antiferromagnets possessing ferromagnet-like responses that are odd in the Néel vector, making X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) a natural probe of ground state altermagnetic order. Because the relativistic ingredient of XMCD at the $L$-edge is supplied predominantly by core-level spin--orbit coupling (SOC), the dichroic signal can reflect the non-relativistic order of the valence electrons. Here we develop a complete symmetry framework for XMCD in altermagnets (AMs) preserving the crystalline unit cell. We tabulate the symmetry-allowed optical Hall vector, anisotropic magnetic dipole (AMD), and underlying octupolar components for all magnetic point groups, thereby identifying the experimental geometries that maximize the XMCD signal. We show that only twelve magnetic point groups, none with a rotation axis of order three or higher, are compatible with both altermagnetism and finite XMCD. By extending the Landau theory of collinear AMs, we connect these relativistic constraints to the spin--orbit-free order. We show that the AMD is forced to vanish at zero valence SOC in conventional antiferromagnets, and that every AM sublattice structure allows the Hall vector and AMD at linear or cubic order in the Néel vector; whether the resulting XMCD is nonzero depends on the Néel vector orientation at finite SOC. The Landau theory thus fixes the Néel-vector dependence of the XMCD for all AM candidates, and separates $d$-wave AMs, whose signal is inherited from a non-relativistic AMD, from $g$- and $i$-wave AMs, whose signal requires valence SOC or core--valence multiplet effects. We illustrate these predictions with first-principles Bethe--Salpeter calculations of $L$-edge XMCD for five representative altermagnetic materials and one conventional antiferromagnet.

papers.abstract: Inversion symmetry forbids bulk second-order spin photocurrents driven solely by electric-dipole coupling. We show that interference between the electric-dipole and spin Zeeman couplings of light enables Zeeman spin-shift and spin-injection currents in centrosymmetric magnets. Our microscopic theory and systematic symmetry analysis establish the allowed responses and polarization selection rules for both spin-degenerate and spin-split antiferromagnets, with and without spin--orbit coupling (SOC). In collinear magnets without SOC, spin injection vanishes, whereas a pure spin-shift current survives independently of the carrier scattering time. This response arises from transverse electronic spin coherences generated by the optical magnetic field, while the ordered moments remain collinear and fixed. Model analyses validate the mechanism, and first-principles calculations for $\mathrm{MnF_2}$ predict experimentally accessible spin photocurrents. These findings establish a general framework for optical spin-current generation in centrosymmetric magnets, including a SOC-free pure-spin mechanism particularly relevant to altermagnets.

papers.abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect provides chiral edge states without the need for an external magnetic field, but unlike in conventional quantum Hall systems, their trajectories cannot be readily controlled electrostatically. Here, we engineer Coulomb interactions between two spatially separated, counter-propagating QAH edge channels using a floating metallic island. Microwave measurements reveal frequency-dependent redistribution of injected edge plasmons between two output channels, demonstrating interaction-induced hybridization of the collective modes. papers.abstract: Twisted oxide double layers have emerged as a promising platform for exploring moiré physics, including polar topologies and emergent electronic phases. However, the intrinsic complexity of oxide surfaces, such as contamination, roughness, and the presence of two distinct terminations (AO and BO2), can complicate the identification of buried interfacial structures. Here, using atomically flat SrTiO3 membranes with a predominantly SrO-TiO2 interfacial configuration, we directly visualize a moiré-periodic structural reconstruction at the buried interface that is distinct from the geometric moiré of rigid stacking. The reconstructed interface hosts head-to-head-like polar distortions, moiré-modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance in otherwise paraelectric and insulating SrTiO3. Our work demonstrates that, with a well-defined termination, moiré reconstruction could serve as a route to emergent electrical behavior in twisted perovskite oxides.

papers.abstract: Recent transport experiments in rhombohedral multilayer graphene have reported evidence for metallic Wigner crystals (mWCs), characterized by the coexistence of crystalline order and a small density of hole-like carriers. This coexistence raises fundamental questions about the stability of mWCs and the fate of their collective excitations in the presence of gapless fermions. Using self-consistent Hartree-Fock and time-dependent Hartree-Fock calculations, we demonstrate that itinerant carriers profoundly influence both. We find that mWCs with electron pockets are generally unstable to particle-hole fluctuations, while hole-doped mWCs at lower densities remain locally stable. In the stable hole-doped mWC, the longitudinal phonon strongly hybridizes with particle-hole excitations, while the transverse phonon remains relatively well defined. Quasiparticle coupling is strongly mode-dependent and is typically stronger for longitudinal-like excitations than for transverse modes. Our results demonstrate that self-doped carriers not only enable metallicity but also fundamentally reshape the stability, collective dynamics, and quasiparticle interactions of electronic crystals.

papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent discovery of unconventional surface superconductivity in PtBi$_{2}$, we theoretically study its signatures in the Little-Parks oscillations of a narrow ring made from the same material. Using a Ginzburg-Landau model with three coupled pairing channels allowed by the trigonal crystal symmetry, we show that a fixed in-plane magnetic field can make the mean-field transition temperature asymmetric under reversal of the normal flux through the ring, while preserving periodicity in the superconducting flux quantum. The leading weak-field contribution to this asymmetry is cubic in the in-plane field strength. The flux-odd component respects the threefold crystal symmetry and changes sign when the in-plane field is rotated by $π/3$ at fixed magnitude. Within the homogeneous ring model, this asymmetry is absent for a single pairing channel and arises from the coupling between the three channels. Our calculations further show that increasing the in-plane magnetic field can enhance the superconducting nucleation temperature through mixing of pairing channels, illustrating magnetic control of multicomponent superconductivity in mesoscopic rings. Little-Parks interferometry with independent control of flux and field direction thus offers a mesoscopic probe of the pairing state, complementary to spectroscopic studies of the gap structure.

However, the respective energy scale is well below the value prescribed by a single-island geometric capacitances. We explain it by strong quantum fluctuations of charge associated with a large value of Josephson energy, $E_J\gg E_C$, where $E_C$ is the charging energy associated with the inter-island capacitance. Comparison between the data and theory points to an exponential (in parameter $E_J/E_C$) suppression of the threshold. We achieve a quantitative agreement with theory by accounting for charge-$e$ solitons associated with the quasiparticles entering the array from its leads. This scenario however underestimates the current below threshold in comparison with the experiment.

But accurately determining the orbital electron or hole occupations in these systems remains a difficult and unresolved task. papers.abstract: Fractional Chern insulators realize fractional quantum Hall states without external magnetic fields, while their underlying lattice periodicity allows otherwise dispersionless anyons to acquire finite bandwidth. Here we show that flux--lattice commensurability can also give rise to multiple anyon bands with nontrivial topology and symmetry-protected connectivity. In multiband vortexable systems, commensurability between the lattice periodicity and the effective magnetic unit cell of fractionally charged quasiholes leads to the folding of a quasihole Landau level into multiple bands. Interactions lift their degeneracy, producing dispersive bands with Chern numbers distinct from that of the parent quasihole Landau level. We further demonstrate that these Chern numbers can be redistributed through Dirac crossings under continuous deformations that preserve exact electronic flatness, while crystalline symmetries can enforce protected band touchings. Our results establish that fractionalized excitations can exhibit the rich band topology familiar from electronic Bloch bands, opening possibilities for nontrivial anyon dynamics beyond conventional Landau-level physics.

papers.abstract: Monolayer FeSe and Fe(Te,Se) grown on SrTiO$_3$ exhibit some of the highest superconducting transition temperatures among iron-based superconductors, yet their pairing mechanism and symmetry remain elusive. Motivated by the recent surprising discovery of nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM) [T. Wei et al., arXiv:2610.38421 (2026)], we investigate superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$3$ (1L-FeSe/STO) within an extended Hubbard model incorporating both onsite and intersite Coulomb interactions among Fe $3d$ and Se $4p$ orbitals. We show that Fe-Se intersite Coulomb repulsion strongly enhances small-momentum $p$-$d$ charge-transfer fluctuations, which mediate attractive intraorbital spin-singlet pairing interactions. These electronic fluctuations may be further enhanced by forward-scattering optical phonons of the SrTiO$3$ substrate. The resulting intrapocket attraction, together with residual repulsive interpocket interactions, stabilizes a mirror-odd, nodeless $B_{1g}$ ($d$-wave) superconducting state with opposite gap signs on the two electron pockets. Both Fe $t_{2g}$ and Se $4p$ orbitals contribute substantially to this multiorbital superconductivity. The calculated superconducting gap and density of states exhibit a two-peak structure, while the Josephson tunneling conductance displays a half-lattice-period modulation, in excellent agreement with experimental observations. Our results establish electronic charge-transfer fluctuations as a viable pairing mechanism for unconventional nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/STO.

papers.abstract: Noncoplanar magnetic orders carry a scalar spin chirality, and their melting by quantum fluctuations has been proposed as a route to chiral spin liquids. We ask what this route can produce on the square-kagome lattice, where couplings across the octagons stabilize noncoplanar cuboc and conical orders. We classify the fermionic spin liquids of this lattice by their projective symmetry groups, identify the symmetry class into which each noncoplanar order would melt, and compare candidate states with Gutzwiller-projected wave functions. A magnetic selection rule constrains the route: the chirality of every cuboc and conical order alternates in space, so a liquid that keeps the symmetry of its parent order has zero Chern number and no spontaneous thermal Hall response. A Chern state can descend only from uniformly chiral orders, and the regular ones we find need ferromagnetic bow-tie couplings. The energetics do not favor a chiral liquid either: among the projected wave functions we compare, a cuboc1-ordered state is lowest for strong cross-octagon couplings, and nonchiral states, a valence-bond crystal or a time-reversal-symmetric liquid, for weaker ones. The two inequivalent site orbits shape the spinons: a relative time-reversal sign between them pins flat bands to the Fermi level, and because the translations of $p4mm$ are not commutators, staggered chiral liquids exist, which are absent on sixfold-symmetric lattices.

papers.abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are prime candidates for future information technology, and their fate in devices is settled by the defects they encounter. In ultrathin films, skyrmions can be as small as a couple of nanometers, carrying only a few tens of magnetic moments, while atomic defects reshape their energy landscape on the atomic scale. Here, we demonstrate that such ultrasmall skyrmions can behave quantum mechanically and that their quantum dynamics is unusual. Since the gyrotropic force dominates, the two coordinates of a ferromagnetic skyrmion are canonically conjugate and the skyrmion behaves as a particle in the lowest Landau level of an effective magnetic field, with a magnetic length of 0.6~Å. Utilizing skyrmion-defect interaction profiles of Cr and Fe adatoms and dimers in PdFe/Ir(111), obtained from atomistic spin simulations parametrized from first principles, we unveil quantized gyrotropic orbits with level spacings of 20--85~$μ$eV, bound not only by pinning defects but also, counter-intuitively, by repulsive ones. Saddle points of the energy landscape act as quantum beam splitters for skyrmions, and quantum depinning reaches rates of 1--100~Hz below the critical current. Embedded impurities, in contrast, bind the skyrmion so strongly that it ceases to behave as a rigid particle, defining a strong-coupling regime. For the Gilbert damping typical of ultrathin films, the quantized levels remain well resolved. The thermal-to-quantum crossover lies between 40 and 160~mK, which is within reach of millikelvin scanning tunneling microscopy, where tip-induced escape statistics and electron spin resonance STM can reveal the quantized gyrotropic motion of skyrmions pinned at defects crafted atom by atom.
papers.physics_advance: Ultrasmall skyrmions can occupy quantized gyrotropic orbits, including states bound by repulsive defects; defect saddle points can act as quantum beam splitters, and the predicted quantum regime is accessible at millikelvin temperatures.
papers.relevance_reason: This theoretical study advances quantum magnetism by predicting experimentally accessible quantum dynamics of ultrasmall magnetic skyrmions interacting with atomic defects.
papers.summary_zh: 这项理论研究提出，原子缺陷环境中的超小磁斯格明子可呈现量子运动，缺陷相互作用能够产生量子化回旋轨道、量子分束和脱钉扎。研究估计热—量子 crossover 温度为 40–160 mK，有望通过毫开尔文扫描隧道显微镜进行探测。
papers.method_en: The authors combine an effective lowest-Landau-level description of skyrmion coordinates with Cr- and Fe-adatom and dimer interaction profiles for PdFe/Ir(111), obtained from first-principles-parameterized atomistic spin simulations. They analyze defect-bound levels, escape processes, and the effects of damping and strong impurity coupling.
papers.method_zh: 作者将斯格明子坐标的有效最低朗道能级描述，与针对 PdFe/Ir(111) 中 Cr、Fe 原子吸附体及二聚体、由第一性原理参数化原子自旋模拟得到的相互作用势结合。研究分析了缺陷束缚能级、逃逸过程，以及阻尼和强杂质耦合的影响。
papers.result_en: The predicted magnetic length is 0.6 Å, and quantized gyrotropic level spacings are 20–85 μeV; both attractive and, counterintuitively, repulsive defects can bind skyrmions. Saddle points are predicted to act as quantum beam splitters, while quantum depinning rates are estimated at 1–100 Hz below the critical current. Typical ultrathin-film Gilbert damping is predicted to leave the levels resolved, whereas embedded impurities can bind skyrmions strongly enough to invalidate the rigid-particle picture.
papers.result_zh: 预测的磁长度为 0.6 Å，量子化回旋能级间距为 20–85 μeV；吸引性缺陷以及反直觉的排斥性缺陷都可能束缚斯格明子。研究预测能量景观中的鞍点可充当量子分束器，并估计临界电流以下的量子脱钉扎速率为 1–100 Hz。典型超薄膜吉尔伯特阻尼下能级仍可分辨，而嵌入式杂质可能造成强束缚，使刚性粒子图像失效。
papers.future_en: The authors identify millikelvin scanning tunneling microscopy as a route to test the predicted crossover, using tip-induced escape statistics and electron-spin-resonance STM to probe quantized motion of atomically defect-pinned skyrmions. Experimental tests of the predicted defect-dependent levels and depinning behavior would further assess the model.
papers.future_zh: 作者指出，可利用毫开尔文扫描隧道显微镜检验所预测的 crossover，并通过针尖诱导逃逸统计和电子自旋共振扫描隧道显微镜探测原子级缺陷钉扎斯格明子的量子化运动。实验测量缺陷依赖的能级和脱钉扎行为，可进一步检验该模型。
papers.tier_reason_en: The work presents a distinctive quantum-dynamics framework with quantitative predictions for defect-bound skyrmions and experimentally accessible signatures. Its significance is compelling, though the abstract describes theoretical predictions rather than an experimental observation.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 该研究提出了独特的斯格明子量子动力学框架，并给出缺陷束缚态的定量预测及可实验检验的信号，具有较强影响力；不过摘要报告的是理论预测，而非实验观测。

It proposes L₂⁻ symmetry for this subleading order and analyzes its coupling to the primary order and strain.

papers.abstract: Recent experiments using strain to probe the charge-density wave (CDW) of 1T-TiSe$_2$ have uncovered additional transitions and broken symmetries inside the CDW state. The elastocaloric effect reveals a second transition below $T_\mathrm{CDW}$, which elastoresistivity shows to be associated with ferroaxial order, breaking all vertical mirror symmetries while preserving inversion. In addition, at even lower temperatures, a diverging nematic susceptibility has been reported through elastoresistivity. In this work, we argue that this rich phenomenology cannot be explained by the standard $L_1^-$ CDW order parameter, and instead requires the existence of a secondary CDW order parameter. Based on symmetry, microscopic, and diffraction considerations, we propose this subleading CDW to have $L_2^-$ symmetry. By analyzing the Landau theory of coupled $L_1^-$ and $L_2^-$ orders in the presence of strain, we reproduce the phase boundaries observed in the elastocaloric measurements and the emergence of ferroaxial order below the CDW transition. Moreover, the model supports a third threefold-rotational symmetry breaking transition at lower temperatures, consistent with the reported divergence of the nematic susceptibility.
papers.physics_advance: A secondary L2− CDW order parameter, coupled to the standard L1− order, can account for ferroaxial order and the observed phase boundaries in 1T-TiSe2, and supports a further low-temperature threefold-symmetry-breaking transition.
papers.relevance_reason: It develops a symmetry-based account of multiple experimentally observed symmetry-breaking transitions in the CDW state of a quantum material.
papers.summary_zh: 本文指出，要解释1T-TiSe₂电荷密度波态中观测到的对称性破缺转变序列，仅有标准L₁⁻序参量并不足够，还需要次级CDW序参量。作者提出该次级序具有L₂⁻对称性，并分析其与主序及应变的耦合。
papers.method_en: The authors combine symmetry, microscopic, and diffraction considerations to identify a candidate secondary order, then analyze coupled L₁⁻ and L₂⁻ orders using Landau theory with strain.
papers.method_zh: 作者结合对称性、微观和衍射方面的考量确定次级序的候选类型，随后利用包含应变的Landau理论分析耦合的L₁⁻与L₂⁻序。
papers.result_en: The coupled-order model reproduces the phase boundaries reported in elastocaloric measurements and yields ferroaxial order below the CDW transition. It also supports a lower-temperature transition that breaks threefold rotational symmetry, consistent with the reported divergence of the nematic susceptibility.
papers.result_zh: 耦合序参量模型再现了弹热测量所报告的相边界，并得到CDW转变以下出现铁轴性序的结果。模型还支持在更低温度发生破坏三重旋转对称性的转变，这与已报告的向列磁化率发散相符。
papers.future_en: Further experimental tests of the proposed L₂⁻ component and the lower-temperature threefold-symmetry-breaking transition could distinguish this account from explanations based on the standard CDW order alone.
papers.future_zh: 进一步实验检验所提出的L₂⁻分量及低温三重对称性破缺转变，可帮助区分这一解释与仅基于标准CDW序的解释。
papers.tier_reason_en: The work offers a symmetry-based explanation of multiple reported transitions and connects a Landau model to experimental phase boundaries, but its central proposal remains a theoretical interpretation of existing phenomenology. PRB/Physical Review Materials is a fitting assessment for this focused materials-theory contribution.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 该工作以对称性为基础解释多个已报告的转变，并将Landau模型与实验相边界联系起来，但核心主张仍是对既有现象学的理论解释。对于这一聚焦的材料理论研究，评为PRB/Physical Review Materials较为合适。

papers.authors: Sankar Das Sarma

papers.abstract: Recent experiments on a wide GaAs quantum well report a fractional quantum Hall state at filling factor ν=1/2 with an unusually large activation gap, a sharp maximum of the gap as a function of density, and a possible transition from the non-Abelian Moore-Read Pfaffian to the Abelian Halperin 331 state. We analyze this system theoretically, with self-consistent subband calculations, exact diagonalization, and a reanalysis of the published transport data. We find that the well has two relevant subbands, that with the second subband frozen out the well most likely has no incompressible state at ν=1/2, that a strict bilayer at the maxima of the charge density does not produce 331, and that an active second subband is essential: the ground state is a paired state of electrons in both subbands, on a continuous path between the Pfaffian and 331, with a neutral gap much larger than that of a one-subband Pfaffian. The position of the state on this path is controlled by electrostatic energies that the accessible system sizes contain only in part, and the standard overlaps do not identify the state at these sizes. Our results are more consistent with a Pfaffian-like state than with 331, but they are not definitive. The transport data do not support the reported magnitude of the gap; the gap we extract is smaller and comparable to the calculated two-subband neutral gap. A benchmark calculation for the Laughlin state at ν=1/3 in the same well provides an experimental test of the electrostatic treatment.
papers.physics_advance: The calculations indicate that an active second subband is essential to the ν=1/2 paired state and yields a larger neutral gap, with the state lying along a path between Pfaffian-like and 331 descriptions.
papers.relevance_reason: The work addresses the nature and energy scale of a fractional quantum Hall state in a semiconductor quantum well, a substantive problem in correlated electronic matter.
papers.summary_zh: 这项理论分析认为，宽 GaAs 量子阱中 ν=1/2 分数量子霍尔态需要第二子带参与，其基态更符合处于 Pfaffian 与 331 描述连续路径上的配对态。作者认为现有结果更支持类 Pfaffian 态，但明确指出有限系统尺寸不足以确定其性质，且输运数据不支持此前报告的能隙大小。
papers.method_en: The study combines self-consistent subband calculations and exact diagonalization with a reanalysis of published transport data. It also compares the proposed electrostatic treatment against a ν=1/3 Laughlin-state benchmark in the same well.
papers.method_zh: 研究结合自洽子带计算、精确对角化及已发表输运数据的重新分析。作者还利用同一量子阱中的 ν=1/3 Laughlin 态作为基准，检验所提出的静电处理。
papers.result_en: The calculations indicate two relevant subbands; with the second subband frozen out, the well most likely has no incompressible ν=1/2 state, while a strict bilayer at the charge-density maxima does not yield the 331 state. An active second subband instead supports a paired state between Pfaffian and 331, with a neutral gap much larger than that of a one-subband Pfaffian. The results favor—but do not definitively establish—a Pfaffian-like state, and the reanalyzed transport data give a smaller gap, comparable to the calculated two-subband neutral gap, rather than supporting the reported magnitude.
papers.result_zh: 计算表明有两个相关子带；冻结第二子带时，量子阱很可能没有 ν=1/2 不可压缩态，而在电荷密度峰值处构造严格双层也不会产生 331 态。若第二子带参与，系统则支持 Pfaffian 与 331 之间的配对态，其中性隙远大于单子带 Pfaffian 的中性隙。结果更支持但不能确证类 Pfaffian 态；重新分析的输运数据给出的能隙更小，且与计算所得双子带中性隙相当，不支持此前报告的能隙大小。
papers.future_en: The authors propose measuring the ν=1/3 Laughlin state in the same well as a test of the electrostatic treatment. Larger accessible system sizes and further transport-gap measurements could help resolve the state’s position along the Pfaffian–331 path and test the gap discrepancy.
papers.future_zh: 作者提出，可在同一量子阱中测量 ν=1/3 Laughlin 态，以检验静电处理。更大规模的可计算系统以及进一步的输运能隙测量，有助于确定该态在 Pfaffian–331 路径上的位置，并检验能隙差异。
papers.tier_reason_en: The paper offers a careful, technically substantial analysis of an important fractional quantum Hall problem, but its central state identification remains nondefinitive because of finite-size limitations and the abstract reports no new experimental resolution.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 论文对重要的分数量子霍尔问题进行了严谨且技术含量较高的分析；但受有限尺寸限制，核心态的鉴定仍不确定，摘要也未报告新的实验性定论。
